sections.h2: What is Malden, Massachusetts, like as a place to own a home?
sections.html:
Malden is a compact, dense city in Middlesex County, just north of Boston across the Mystic River. It covers about 5.1 square miles and had 66,263 residents at the 2020 census, which works out to roughly 13,000 people per square mile.

Malden borders Melrose to the north, Medford to the west, Everett to the south, Revere to the east and Saugus to the northeast. Its high ground is Boojum Rock in the Middlesex Fells Reservation, at about 275 feet, and the Malden River drains the city.

Fewer than half of Malden homes are owner occupied, so renting is common here. If you own a house with tenants, tell the buyer up front.

sections.h2: How is Malden organized into squares and neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Malden grew around squares at its crossroads, and many neighborhoods take the name of the square at their center.

  • Squares: Malden Square at Main and Pleasant Streets, Converse Square, Oak Grove Square at the Oak Grove station, Bellrock Square, Judson Square, Maplewood Square and Linden Square.
  • Neighborhoods: Faulkner, West End, Edgeworth, Linden, Ferryway, Forestdale, Maplewood, Bellrock and Belmont Hill.
  • Landmarks by area: Bell Rock Memorial Park and the New England Coffee headquarters in Bellrock, Macdonald Stadium in Edgeworth, and Pine Banks Park shared with Melrose.

Maplewood has a clear origin: in 1847 the president of the Saugus Branch Railroad bought 200 acres and planned wide streets with ornamental trees, and the maples he planted gave the area its name. Edgeworth was once the site of the Converse Rubber Factory, the original home of the Converse sneaker.

sections.h2: What is the history of Malden?
sections.html:
Puritans settled Malden in 1640, the town was incorporated in 1649, and it became a city in 1882.

The area was first called the Mistick Side and was part of Charlestown. It once included Melrose, which separated in 1850, and Everett, which separated in 1870. Malden's first mayor, Elisha S. Converse, funded the Converse Memorial Library, designed by Henry Hobson Richardson and built in 1885.

The Malden High and Medford High Thanksgiving football game dates to 1889 and is the second oldest continuous high school football rivalry in the country. The Saugus Branch railroad line now carries the Northern Strand Trail, a multi-use path that opened in December 2012 and passes through the middle of the city.

For a seller, this long history usually means older housing. A house built a century or more ago can come with original layouts, older heating systems and decades of deferred work.

sections.h2: How do you commute from Malden?
sections.html:
Malden is on the MBTA Orange Line, with stops at Malden Center and Oak Grove, and Malden Center is also a commuter rail stop.

  • U.S. Route 1 is the one limited access route through the city, linking Boston and the North Shore.
  • Routes 28, 60 and 99 run through Malden as arterial roads.
  • Route 16 and Interstate 93 are a short distance outside the city line.
  • MBTA buses reach every adjacent community.

The Northern Strand Trail, also called the Bike to the Sea trail, now gives a paved route from the Mystic River in Everett to Western Avenue in Lynn. Houses within walking distance of Malden Center or Oak Grove draw commuters, which is helpful for a listing, but a cash buyer will price a house on its condition and numbers either way.

Malden Public Schools is the local district, with five elementary and middle schools, one public high school and one public preschool.

The elementary schools Beebe, Ferryway, Forestdale, Linden and Salemwood were replaced with new buildings in the late 1990s. The city's high schools are Malden High School, Malden Catholic High School and Mystic Valley Regional Charter High School. The Cheverus Catholic School serves pre-K through eighth grade.

A National Center for Education Statistics study in 2013 found Malden High to be the most diverse public high school in Massachusetts. Ask your local school office about enrollment boundaries for a specific street, since this page does not list them.

sections.h2: What parks and community services does Malden have?
sections.html:
Malden has about 30 park sites, and open space is a selling point for houses near them.

  • 56 acres of the Middlesex Fells Reservation lie inside the city.
  • Fellsmere Pond covers 25 acres, and the DCR runs a swimming pool.
  • MacDonald Stadium has a 400 meter synthetic running track.
  • The Malden YMCA finished construction in early 2007.
  • The ArtLine, a series of murals and sculptures, runs along the Northern Strand Trail.

Services reflect the city's makeup. Recent immigrants have come largely from Brazil, China, Haiti, India, Morocco and Pakistan, and groups such as the Immigrant Learning Center and the Tri-City Community Action Program serve residents. South Cove Community Health Center began building a Malden site in 2017. Sellers who need to relocate within Malden or nearby can use that network of services when planning a move.

sections.h2: What do sellers need to do before closing on a Malden house?
sections.html:
The Massachusetts Department of Fire Services requires a certificate of compliance from the local fire department showing that your smoke and carbon monoxide alarms meet the standard for a sale or transfer.

The state's steps are practical. Find out when your home was built and when the last building permit was issued, since the alarm requirements depend on those dates. List every alarm and check its manufacture date, because an alarm with no date has expired. Then call the fire department when you have a closing date. The department charges a fee for the inspection and certificate.

Other state costs apply as well. The deed excise under Chapter 64D, Section 1, is two dollars for each five hundred dollars of the sale price, or fraction of it, outside Barnstable County. Massachusetts also keeps deeds in county registries, and most properties are recorded land. Ask the City of Malden's building and assessing offices about permits and bills tied to your address.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale of a Malden house work?
sections.html:
In a cash sale the buyer does not need a mortgage, so the timeline depends on the title work and on when you want to close.

  1. Tell the buyer about the house, any tenants and your timeline.
  2. The buyer reviews the property and presents a written offer.
  3. Once you accept, a Massachusetts attorney handles title and the purchase and sale agreement.
  4. Smoke and CO certification and any payoffs are arranged.
  5. The deed is recorded and you receive the proceeds.

Listing the same house means preparing it, showing it and waiting on a buyer's loan. Selling for cash trades a possible higher price for speed and certainty. For a Malden multifamily with tenants or an estate house full of belongings, that trade is worth thinking through.

faqs.q: How many people live in Malden, MA?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 66,263 residents in Malden, in 26,024 households. About 47.2 percent of housing units were owner occupied.

faqs.q: Is the Orange Line close to most Malden homes?
faqs.a: Malden has two stations, Malden Center and Oak Grove, and the city covers only about five square miles. Many streets are a short walk, bus ride or drive from one of them.

faqs.q: Do I need a certificate for smoke and CO alarms in Malden?
faqs.a: Yes, the Department of Fire Services says a certificate of compliance from the local fire department is needed when you sell or transfer a home. Call the Malden fire department for its fee and scheduling.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Malden two family with tenants?
faqs.a: Yes. Tell the buyer about the leases and rents at the start. Under the contract you can negotiate whether the house closes occupied or vacant, and a Massachusetts attorney can advise you on tenant notice rules.

faqs.q: What does the Massachusetts deed excise tax cost?
faqs.a: It is two dollars per five hundred dollars of the price or fraction of it. On a $600,000 sale that is $2,400. Your contract and attorney will confirm who pays it.
